name: v9.1.0
body:
## obsidian-mind 9.1: sessions keep their goals, and upgrades keep your changes

## Highlights

- **Start every session with your goals, even with a long North Star.**
  When the hook budget is tight, sections now shrink step by step instead of vanishing:
  1. full North Star
  2. Current Focus only
  3. one headline per goal
  4. the goals that fit
  5. a pointer to the file

  The size line names whatever was shrunk. Before, 30 long goals arrived as a bare pointer. Now all 30 arrive as headlines. This is the path Codex, Gemini and older Claude Code use.
- **Upgrade with `/om-vault-upgrade`.** Run it with no arguments; it works through ShardMind 0.2.1. Before changing anything, it shows each file that differs from the template:
  - **behind:** takes the new version;
  - **ahead:** keeps yours, and flags it as worth upstreaming;
  - **merged** or **conflict:** for you to review.
- **Lean on two new test gates:** every anchored `promoted:` marker must resolve, and no note may hold hard-wrapped prose.

## Before you upgrade

- **Update ShardMind to 0.2.1 or later first:** `npm install -g shardmind@latest`.
  ShardMind 0.2.0 can delete a clone's `.shardmind/` files when `adopt` fails or is cancelled, and `/om-vault-upgrade` runs `adopt`, so older versions are now refused. Already hit by it? Run `git checkout -- .shardmind`.
- **Fix what the new gates flag in your own `npm test`.** Re-point `promoted:` markers after a note split, as `/om-tidy` describes. Unwrap hard-wrapped paragraphs, or mark a raw capture `verbatim: true` (or drop a `.verbatim` file in its folder).
- **Expect more write warnings.** The hook now applies `frontmatter_required` from `vault-manifest.json`: work notes need `quarter` and `status`, 1:1 notes `quarter`, people `title`, and main incident notes `ticket`, `severity` and `role`. They are warnings only, and the Work Note template gains `quarter:`.
- **Delete old test leftovers if you have them:** `session-start-*` files in `~/.cache/qmd` and `~/.config/qmd`. `npm test` now keeps qmd's files out of your folders and fails if a test writes there.
- **Start Codex and Gemini sessions from the vault root on Windows.** Their hooks now find their scripts there; a session started in a subfolder still doesn't (#302).

## Built on 9.0: the vault rides inside Claude Code

Hooks have limits nobody sees. Claude Code cuts their output at 10,000 characters, compaction shrinks the session context to a pointer, and subagents never get it. 9.0 added a **Claude Code mod**: same vault, same scripts, a better way in.

- **Session context arrives as an instruction file**, the way `CLAUDE.md` does. It survives `/compact` and `/clear`, reaches subagents, and gets its own 20,000-byte budget (`eager_layer_instruction_budget_bytes`). `/memory` lists it as `.claude/session-context.md`.
- **The Stop report is one line under the answer.** Claude gets the full report with your next message, once per change.
- **Hooks work after `/cd`.** Every hook finds the vault root from a subfolder.

A delivery gate asks the model itself what it received: at startup, after `/compact` and `/clear`, and from a subagent. "It works" is measured, not assumed.

**Nothing breaks if you don't use it.** Codex, Gemini, Claude Code before 2.1.287 and untrusted folders run the hooks as before; the mod loads only after you accept Claude Code's trust prompt. It runs with your permissions, so read what it does first with `claude plugin validate .claude/skills/obsidian-mind`. To turn it off, add `"enabledPlugins": { "obsidian-mind@skills-dir": false }` to `.claude/settings.local.json`.

Full 9.0 notes: [v9.0.0](https://github.com/breferrari/obsidian-mind/releases/tag/v9.0.0).

---

## Quick Start

**Requirements:** [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md), [Node 22+ LTS](https://nodejs.org), and one of: [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) · [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) · [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli)

**Install via [ShardMind](https://github.com/breferrari/shardmind) (recommended — wizard, optional modules, managed upgrades):**

```bash
npm install -g shardmind
mkdir my-vault && cd my-vault
shardmind install github:breferrari/obsidian-mind
```

**Or clone directly:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/breferrari/obsidian-mind.git
cd obsidian-mind
npm install -g @tobilu/qmd && qmd index && qmd embed   # optional: semantic search
```

Open the folder as an Obsidian vault, then run `claude`, `codex`, or `gemini` in the directory and type `/om-standup` (or `om-standup` in Codex).

Or download the vault zip below and extract it into your Obsidian vaults folder.

**Already using obsidian-mind?** Just tell your agent: `Update this vault to the latest obsidian-mind from https://github.com/breferrari/obsidian-mind`

## v9.1.0 — 2026-10-06

### Added
- make /om-vault-upgrade ShardMind-aware, keeping local improvements through an upgrade
- add a prose-width rule so vaults stop teaching sessions to hard wrap
- gate every anchored promoted marker on resolving, and retarget markers on a split

### Fixed
- run the release job's tests as CI does, and stop two Stop tests depending on qmd
- require shardmind 0.2.1 so a failed adopt cannot delete a clone's .shardmind files
- run Codex and Gemini hooks on Windows by a relative script path
- deliver every live goal at North Star's full level, and report any cut in the meter
- degrade eager-layer sections by levels instead of collapsing them whole
- resolve the QMD store path the way qmd does, honouring INDEX_PATH
- keep the test suite from writing QMD stores and configs into the user's folders
- enforce every tool's schema required fields in the MCP dispatcher
- link an informed_by title holding # or | by basename so the link resolves
- drive the frontmatter write check from frontmatter_required in the manifest
- drop backticks from memory filenames so a wikilink to them resolves
- refuse a record_work call with no title instead of writing an undefined note
- flag mcp_never_expose entries that are paths or folders instead of ignoring them
- derive the auto-memory directory on Windows so tidy-fix migrates strays there
- add a trailing flush so edits inside the QMD refresh debounce window get indexed
- report tidy-fix moves as fixed only when they succeed
- prefer a runnable qmd install over the first one that merely exists
- fail charcount when the section is not found, and match ## headings
